entries.name: PID (DBL) VI
entries.description: Implements a PID controller using a PID algorithm for simple PID applications or high speed control applications that require an efficient algorithm. The PID algorithm features control output range limiting with integrator anti-windup and bumpless controller output for PID gain changes. Use the DBL instance of this VI to implement a single control loop. Use the DBL Array instance to implement parallel multi-loop control. Functions 5716 ni.com

terminals.name: output range
terminals.description: output range specifies the range to which to coerce the control output. The default range is –100 to 100, which corresponds to values specified in terms of percentage of full scale.

terminals.name: output low
terminals.description: output low specifies the minimum value of the controller output. The default is –100.

terminals.name: setpoint
terminals.description: setpoint specifies the setpoint value, or desired value, of the process variable being controlled.

terminals.name: process variable
terminals.description: process variable specifies the measured value of the process variable being controlled. This value is equal to the feedback value of the feedback control loop.

terminals.name: PID gains
terminals.description: PID gains specifies the proportional gain, integral time, and derivative time parameters of the controller.

terminals.name: integral time (Ti, min)
terminals.description: integral time (Ti, min) specifies the integral time in minutes. The default is 0.01.

terminals.name: derivative time (Td, min)
terminals.description: derivative time (Td, min) specifies the derivative time in minutes. The default is 0.

terminals.name: dt (s)
terminals.description: dt (s) specifies the loop-cycle time, or interval in seconds, at which this VI is called. If dt (s) is less than or equal to zero, this VI calculates the time since it was last called using an internal timer with 1 ms resolution. If dt (s) must be less than 1 ms, specify the value explicitly. The default is -1.

terminals.name: reinitialize? (F)
terminals.description: reinitialize? specifies whether to reinitialize the internal parameters, such as the integrated error, of the controller. Set reinitialize? to TRUE if your application must stop and restart the control loop without restarting the entire application. The default is FALSE.

terminals.name: output
terminals.description: output returns the control output of the PID algorithm that is applied to the controlled process. If this VI receives an invalid input, output returns NaN .

terminals.name: dt out (s)
terminals.description: dt out (s) returns the actual time interval in seconds. dt out (s) returns either the value of dt (s) or the computed interval if you set dt (s) to –1.

terminals.description: hold specifies whether the controller ignores changes in the process variable and suspends any integral action. If you set hold as TRUE, output will retain its previous value. The default is FALSE.

entries.name: PID Advanced (DBL) VI
entries.description: Implements a PID controller using a PID algorithm with advanced optional features. The advanced PID algorithm includes the features of the algorithm the PID VI uses, as well as manual mode control with bumpless manual-to-automatic transitions, nonlinear integral action, two degree-of-freedom control, and error-squared control. Use the DBL instance of this VI to implement a single control loop. Use the DBL Array instance to implement parallel multi-loop control. Functions © National Instruments 5

terminals.name: alpha
terminals.description: alpha specifies the derivative filter time constant. Increasing this value increases damping of derivative action.

terminals.name: gamma
terminals.description: gamma specifies an amount by which to weight the error applied to derivative action. The default value is 0, which avoids the derivative kick , or sudden change in controller output, that can occur after a change in the setpoint value. In certain cascade control operations where derivative kick is not a concern, increasing gamma might improve the speed of the first PID controller.

entries.name: PID Gain Schedule (DBL) VI
entries.description: Selects a set of PID gains from a gain schedule for the control of processes that require different sets of gains for different regions of operation, such as highly nonlinear processes. Use the DBL instance of this VI to implement a single control loop. Use the DBL Array instance to implement parallel multi-loop control.

terminals.name: gain scheduling value
terminals.description: gain scheduling value specifies the current input value to use to select PID gains from the gain schedule.

terminals.name: PID gain schedule
terminals.description: PID gain schedule specifies the gain schedule for the proportional, integral, and derivative gain parameters. Specify the maximum values for the PID gain schedule in ascending order. This VI uses the first set of PID gains in the array for all gain scheduling values less than the corresponding maximum value. If you define a maximum setpoint value and the actual setpoint rises above that value, this VI continues to behave as if the maximum setpoint value were still in effect.

terminals.name: max value
terminals.description: max value specifies the maximum value of the range of the gain scheduling value.

terminals.name: index out
terminals.description: index out returns the index of the element in the PID gain schedule array corresponding to the PID gains out output.

terminals.name: PID gains out
terminals.description: PID gains out returns the current PID gains from the gain schedule.
